neighbours.label: punctuation that opens an explanatory gloss or clarification (' (' before 'such as'/'the ...', 'i.e.', em dash)
fire: Some animals rely on chemical signals (such as scent markings) to find a mate.
The value must be positive (i.e., greater than zero) for the formula to work.
Many people struggle with procrastination—putting off tasks until the last minute.
The reaction needs a catalyst (a substance that speeds it up) to proceed.
Most plants need macronutrients (nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium) to grow well.
Each node stores a pointer to its parent (the node directly above it) in the tree.
The author favours empirical methods—those based on observation—over theory.
Young birds keep gaining weight until departure (i.e., they show no plateau).
quiet: Some animals rely on chemical signals to find a mate in the dark forest.
The value must be greater than zero for the formula to work.
Many people struggle with procrastination and put off tasks until the last minute.
The reaction needs a catalyst that speeds it up in order to proceed.
Most plants need nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium to grow well.
Each node stores a pointer to the node directly above it in the tree.
The author favours methods based on observation over pure theory.
Young birds keep gaining weight until departure and show no plateau.

notes: card: ' (' x11, '.' x6, '—' x3, '.e' x2 in definitional text. Quiet: same definitions stated without a parenthetical/dash gloss.
